about: Into the West End. Knightsbridge in the morning, Mayfair, lunch near Piccadilly Circus, then down Whitehall.

cards.line: Did you know, the Beatles played their last ever gig on a rooftop in Savile Row?
cards.fact: On 30 January 1969 the Beatles played on the roof of their Apple offices at 3 Savile Row. After 42 minutes, police told them to turn it down. They never played in public again.

cards.line: Did you know, Whitehall Palace had a screen so passers-by couldn't see the king in his bath?
cards.fact: The king's rooms at Whitehall Palace looked over the Privy Garden. A screen stopped people walking past from seeing him naked in his bathtub.
cards.source: Wikipedia: Privy Garden of the Palace of Whitehall

cards.line: Did you know, the Old War Office on Whitehall played MI6 in Bond films?
cards.fact: In three 1980s Bond films, the Old War Office on Whitehall stood in for MI6's headquarters. The real MI6 is across the river at Vauxhall Cross.
cards.source: Wikipedia: War Office; bondlocations.com (MI6 tag); jamesbondlifestyle.com: SIS/MI6 Headquarters, Vauxhall Cross

cards.line: Did you know, Jimi Hendrix lived next door to Handel's house on Brook Street?
cards.fact: Jimi Hendrix lived at 23 Brook Street in 1968 and 1969. Next door, at number 25, the composer Handel had lived from 1723 until 1759. Today the two houses are one museum.

cards.line: Did you know, An American Werewolf in London was the first film in 15 years allowed to shoot in Piccadilly Circus?
cards.fact: In 1981, An American Werewolf in London became the first film allowed to shoot in Piccadilly Circus in 15 years.
cards.source: Wikipedia: An American Werewolf in London

about: A day in the City, then a walk east along the river to Wapping and over to Rotherhithe.

cards.line: Did you know, a courier was mugged for £292 million on Nicholas Lane?
cards.fact: In 1990 a courier was mugged on Nicholas Lane and lost £292 million in bearer bonds, which pay whoever holds them. Police got back all but two of the 301 certificates.

cards.line: Did you know, the first sans serif type with lower-case letters was made on Fann Street?
cards.fact: William Thorowgood of the Fann Street Foundry designed the first sans serif type with lower-case letters: plain letters, without the little strokes at their ends. He called it Grotesque.

cards.line: Did you know, Dick Whittington gave London a toilet with 128 seats?
cards.fact: Dick Whittington paid for a public toilet by the Thames with 128 seats, 64 for men and 64 for women. The tide washed it out twice a day.

cards.line: Did you know, pirates were hanged at Wapping and left until three tides had washed over them?
cards.fact: For over 400 years pirates were hanged at Execution Dock in Wapping, just past the low-tide mark. Their bodies were left until at least three tides had washed over their heads.

cards.line: Did you know, a house by the Thames in Rotherhithe is nicknamed the Leaning Tower?
cards.fact: 1 Fulford Street, a house nicknamed the Leaning Tower of Rotherhithe, was once a wages office. Bargemen pulled their barges up alongside it to collect their pay.

about: Marylebone and north: Baker Street, Lord's, St John's Wood, home past Primrose Hill.

cards.line: Did you know, a 1971 bank raid on Baker Street was overheard on a radio half a mile away?
cards.fact: In 1971 a gang tunnelled into the Lloyds Bank vault on Baker Street from a shop two doors away. A radio fan half a mile off heard their walkie-talkies. Police thought it was a prank.

cards.line: Did you know, London's first railway tunnel runs under Primrose Hill?
cards.fact: The tunnel under Primrose Hill was London's first railway tunnel, dug for the London and Birmingham Railway in the 1830s. Its entrances have barely changed since.

cards.line: Did you know, the Abbey Road cover was shot in ten minutes while a policeman held up the traffic?
cards.fact: The Beatles' Abbey Road cover was taken on the zebra crossing outside the studios on 8 August 1969. The photographer stood on a stepladder and had ten minutes, while a policeman held up the traffic.

cards.line: Did you know, Britain's first heart transplant happened on Westmoreland Street?
cards.fact: In 1968 Donald Ross and his team carried out Britain's first heart transplant on Westmoreland Street, where the National Heart Hospital then stood.

cards.line: Did you know, until 1999 the Queen was the only woman allowed in the Lord's Pavilion during play?
cards.fact: Until 1999, women weren't allowed in the Lord's Pavilion during play. The one exception was the Queen, the club's patron.

about: Driving: through Sutton, up to Battersea, Knightsbridge and Earl's Court, out west to Acton.

cards.line: Did you know, Pink Floyd's giant pig broke loose from Battersea Power Station and flew over Heathrow?
cards.fact: In December 1976 a giant inflatable pig was flown between Battersea Power Station's chimneys for a Pink Floyd album cover. It broke free, flew over Heathrow, grounded flights and landed in Kent.

cards.line: Did you know, Batman's chemical works was a power station in Acton?
cards.fact: The disused Acton Lane power station was a film set twice: for Aliens in 1986, and as Axis Chemical Works in the 1989 Batman.

cards.line: Did you know, the Kray twins once owned a Knightsbridge nightclub?
cards.fact: From 1960 to 1963 the Kray twins owned Esmeralda's Barn, a nightclub on Wilton Place in Knightsbridge. The gangsters used it to move their business into the West End.

cards.line: Did you know, the Rolling Stones became a five-piece in a Sutton pub?
cards.fact: The Rolling Stones played gigs at the Red Lion on Sutton High Street, now the Winning Post. It was there, in January 1963, that Charlie Watts and Bill Wyman joined the band for good.

cards.line: Did you know, Bob Marley gave police a false address on Collingham Gardens?
cards.fact: When Bob Marley was arrested for cannabis in 1977, he gave police an address on Collingham Gardens. It wasn't his home: he gave it to keep police away from where he lived, on Oakley Street.
